correctness.rationale: Spectral-compression sum-of-squares identity holds with degenerate projectors. The three-dimensional bright quotient has simple nonzero eigenvalues for every nonzero potential. Its diagonal moment determinant equals minus the potential times the unmarked-part size and is nonzero. The zero dark projector decomposes into two independent cell-contrast projectors; their compressions yield exactly the size-two exceptions. At zero potential the separate two-cell bright/dark argument gives the claimed boundary formula. The exact-rational symmetric-commutant verifier confirmed 100 profiles but is not substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: A localized diagonal defect is the standard mathematical model of a marked search vertex. The exact infinite-family classification displays all three genuinely distinct rank responses (up, down, unchanged) under an arbitrarily weak nonzero mark, with explicit kernels and sharp positivity criteria. This is not a parameter substitution or a numerical census: it identifies spectral multiplicity and dark-mode mechanisms governing long-time quantum transport.
